note: The published species-level models of research effort and what each reports for threat status once its other covariates are in. 'read' says whether the threat-term result was read from the full text, from the abstract only, or not at all. Verified 5 September 2026; quotes are verbatim.

models.citation: Brooke, Bielby, Nambiar & Carbone 2014, PLoS ONE 9:e93195
models.response: papers per species, Web of Science 1900-2010
models.covariates: body mass, range size, diet breadth, family, IUCN status
models.quote: IUCN threat status did not exhibit a strong relationship with research effort which suggests that the conservation needs of individual species are not major drivers of research interest.
models.label: Brooke et al. 2014

models.covariates: range, migration, generation length, clutch size, habitat breadth, body mass; phylogeny and realm as random effects (74% of variance to phylogeny)
models.threat_term: Least Concern 31.4 +/- 1.4 papers vs threatened 14.5 +/- 0.9, Wilcoxon p < 0.001; threat status is not a term of the final phylogenetic model
models.quote: research effort was twice as high for species of 'Least Concern' status as for threatened species
models.label: Ducatez & Lefebvre 2014

models.response: papers and h-index per species, Web of Science 1972-2014
models.covariates: population size, guild, native status, UK Biodiversity Action Plan status, breeding status, Red List status
models.threat_term: Red List status: total papers chi-squared = 0.92, p = 0.34; h-index chi-squared = 0.82, p = 0.37 (S2 Table). National BAP status positive: t = 3.14, p < 0.005
models.quote: Red List status (international action) did not have any significant impact on either publication metric.
models.aside: the national action-plan listing was a significant positive predictor; the international Red List category was not
models.label: McKenzie & Robertson 2015

models.covariates: current range, taxonomic group, body mass, origin (native/introduced), range change, IUCN status
models.threat_term: not stated in the abstract; the full text is paywalled
models.quote: many Australian native species of conservation significance have attracted little research effort, little recognition, and little funding
models.label: Fleming & Bateman 2016

models.citation: dos Santos et al. 2020, Animal Conservation 23:679-688
models.response: conservation papers per species, Web of Science; hurdle model (presence, then count)
models.covariates: range-country scientific capacity, body mass, years since description, invasiveness, threat status, others
models.threat_term: relative importance not given in the abstract; the full text is paywalled
models.quote: The threat status was weakly associated to explain the presence/absence and research volume in conservation research.
models.label: dos Santos et al. 2020

models.covariates: log body mass, absolute latitude, IUCN status (linear and quadratic), human use, domestication, log Google Trends, phylogeny as random effect (H2 = 0.64)
models.quote: larger mammals that are less endangered could be attracting more research attention than smaller mammals that are severely endangered
models.aside: U-shaped: research falls with rising risk across most of the scale and rises again at the top
models.label: Tam et al. 2022

models.response: papers per species, Web of Science 1945 to sampling; Wikipedia views 2016-2021
models.covariates: organism size, colourfulness, range size, domain, taxonomic uniqueness, common name, IUCN status, human use, harmfulness, phylogenetic distance to humans; taxonomy and region as random effects
models.threat_term: presence on the Red List raises interest; endangered and least concern species both more studied than unlisted (Figure 3A; Supplementary file 1a)
models.quote: both endangered and least concern species were more studied and popular
models.aside: the effect is being assessed at all, not being threatened; the authors note the circularity: assessment needs data
models.label: Mammola et al. 2023

models.response: papers per species, Scopus; negative-binomial mixed models
models.covariates: body size, description year, range overlap with institutions, threat status, human density, range rarity, socioeconomic terms
models.threat_term: not quantified in the abstract; full text (CC BY) could not be fetched past the publisher's bot wall
models.quote: Although we demonstrate that biological and socioeconomic factors more strongly affect reptile research effort variation, geography and conservation-related factors also matter.
models.label: Guedes et al. 2023

models.covariates: flower colour, conspicuousness, range, ecology, rarity
models.threat_term: not readable; the full text is paywalled and the abstract was not retrievable
models.label: Adamo et al. 2021

models.response: papers per species, Web of Science 1975-2023
models.covariates: range size, introduction status, realm, carapace length, egg length; phylogeny (66% of variance)
models.threat_term: extinction risk -0.099 +/- 0.214, t = -0.463, p = 0.644; assessed species more studied than unassessed (p < 0.001)
models.quote: The research effort of threatened and non-threatened species did not differ significantly
models.label: Ducatez & DeVore 2026
